subject: Matemática
description_pt: Associar as representações 10%, 25%, 50%, 75% e 100% respectivamente à décima parte, quarta parte, metade, três quartos e um inteiro, para calcular porcentagens, utilizando estratégias pessoais, cálculo mental e calculadora, em contextos de educação financeira, entre outros.

components.description_pt: Associar porcentagens de referência (10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) com suas formas fracionárias
components.description_en: Associate benchmark percentages (10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) with their equivalent fractional forms
components.cc_component_description: Recognize equivalent fractions using the principle a / b = (n x a)/(n x b) (denominators limited to 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100)

components.description_pt: Calcular uma porcentagem de referência de uma quantidade usando cálculo mental ou calculadora
components.description_en: Calculate a benchmark percentage of a quantity using mental computation or a calculator
components.cc_component_description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100

components.description_pt: Aplicar relações de porcentagem de referência para resolver problemas em contextos de educação financeira
components.description_en: Apply benchmark percentage relationships to solve problems in financial literacy contexts
components.cc_component_description: Multiply rational numbers to solve mathematical problems

cc_matches.description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g., 30% of a quantity means 30/100 times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

Explain why a fraction $\frac{a}{b}$ is equivalent to a fraction $\frac{(n \times a)}{(n \times b)}$ by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.
